preconditions.description: Attacker must hold some JizzJet tokens to trigger the swapAndLiquify function
Contract must have accumulated enough tokens from fees to reach numTokensSellToAddToLiquidity threshold

exploit_hint: The vulnerability is in the sendBNBToAdmin function which uses transfer() without checking the return value. If the admin wallet is a contract that reverts on receive (e.g., has a fallback function that reverts), the entire swapAndLiquify transaction will fail, causing the contract to accumulate tokens but never distribute BNB to the admin. An attacker can exploit this by: 1) Ensuring the admin wallet is a contract that reverts on receive, 2) Triggering swapAndLiquify by making transfers that accumulate fees, 3) The contract will swap tokens for ETH but fail on transfer, leaving ETH stuck in contract, 4) Attacker can then potentially front-run or manipulate to benefit from the stuck ETH.
